questions.ask: Could you tell me your date of birth, please?
What are the last four digits of the mobile number we have on file for you?

hints.day_month_swapped: It looks like the day and the month may be the wrong way round. Could you give me your date of birth again, day first, then month, then year?

lines.opening: Hello, this is Harbour Bank's virtual assistant, and we record this call.
lines.robot: Yes, I'm Harbour Bank's virtual assistant, an automated service.
lines.scam: I understand your caution. I'm Harbour Bank's virtual assistant, and I will never ask for your PIN or passwords. If you prefer, you can call us back on the number on our official website.
lines.purpose_before_verify: I can explain once I've confirmed I'm speaking with the right person. It's just a couple of quick security questions.
lines.no_info: I'm sorry, I can't share that information.
lines.not_talk_once: I understand. This will only take a few minutes. May I continue?
lines.tp_ask: I'm afraid I can't share any details. When would be a good time to reach {title} {last_name}, today or the next business day, between 12 noon and 8 pm?
lines.tp_ask_time: What time would suit, between 12 noon and 8 pm?
lines.tp_outside_window: I'm sorry, I can only call back today or on the next business day, between 12 noon and 8 pm, and later than now. Is there another time that works?
lines.tp_no_info: I'm sorry, I can't share any details. I can only arrange a time to call back.
lines.tp_booked: Thank you. We'll call back on {date} at {time}.
lines.condolence: I'm very sorry for your loss. Thank you for letting me know.
lines.id_intro: Before we go on, I need to ask you two quick security questions.
lines.id_why: These questions protect your privacy, so I only discuss your details with you.
lines.id_explain: I ask these questions to make sure I'm speaking with the right person and to keep your information safe.
lines.id_declined: I understand. Without these answers I can't continue. You can contact us any time through online banking.
lines.id_repeat: Sorry, I didn't catch that. Could you say it again?
lines.id_wrong: I'm sorry, that doesn't match what we have. Let's try that again.
lines.id_failed: I'm sorry, I couldn't confirm your identity, so I can't continue. Please get in touch with us through online banking.
lines.disclose_intro: Thank you. I'm calling about a missed payment.
lines.product_line: Your {name} has {amount} in arrears and is {days} days late.
lines.ask_today: Could you pay the full {amount} today?
lines.ask_today_multi: Could you pay the full amounts today?
lines.offer: Would you be able to pay {amount} by {date}?
lines.offer_floor: If the full amount is too much, the least we can accept is {amount}. Could you manage that?
lines.below_floor: I'm sorry, that's below the minimum we can accept. The minimum is {amount}. Could you manage that?
lines.below_floor_again: I'm sorry, I can't accept less than {amount}.
lines.date_past: That date has already passed. Could you choose a date from today onwards?
lines.not_business_day: That day isn't a business day. The next business day is {date}. Would that work?
lines.after_deadline: I'm sorry, the latest date I can accept is {date}. Could you pay by then?
lines.vague_ask: Which exact day would that be?
lines.ask_date_for_amount: On what date could you pay {amount}?
lines.repeat_offer: Just to repeat, could you pay {amount} by {date}?
lines.readback_intro: Let me read that back to you.
lines.clamped_note: For your {name}, the latest date I can accept is {date}, so I'll use that date.
lines.confirm_q: Shall I go ahead and log that?
lines.recorded: Thank you, your promise has been recorded.
lines.sms_line: You'll get an email confirmation shortly.
lines.record_failed: I'm sorry, our system had a problem and your promise could not be recorded.
lines.paid_line: Thank you for letting me know. Payments can take up to three working days to show on your account.
lines.dispute_line: I understand. I won't ask you for a payment promise today, and the team will look into it.
lines.hardship: I'm really sorry to hear that. Our Customer Care team can help with situations like this. Would you like me to put you through to them?
lines.hardship_declined: I understand. If you change your mind, our Customer Care team is there to help.
lines.restructure_line: Of course. I'll put you through to our team who can talk about a payment plan.
lines.human_ask_help: Of course. Before I transfer you, is there anything I can help you with?
lines.transfer: I'll put you through now. Please hold.
lines.goodbye: Thank you for your time. Goodbye.

assumptions: The memo of 25 September 2026 beats policy v4.2 where they disagree, as Priya's email says.
Security question (b) is the last four digits of the mobile number (memo item 1), not the postcode (7.3). It maps to verify field 'mobile_last4', and question (a), date of birth, maps to 'dob'.
Two wrong security answers in total end the check (memo item 2), not three (7.4). This applies even though the tool API description says three.
The latest promise date is the 10th business day after today (memo item 3). This replaces '14 calendar days after today' (7.7).

Customers more than 30 days late get two persuasion attempts: first the full arrears on the latest allowed date (7.9), then the minimum amount on the latest allowed date (memo item 4). Customers 30 days late or less get one attempt. I set band boundaries at 0-30 and 31 or more days (upper bound 100000 as an open end).
The only hint value in the tool API is 'day_month_swapped'. The brief gives no wording for it, so the agent asks for the date of birth again, day first, to match date_order 'dmy'.
Callbacks are allowed today or the next business day (memo item 5 adds to 7.5), from 12:00 to 20:00 inclusive and strictly after the current time. No callback after two asks in total gives NC-NOCB.
The brief names no currency. I used the default 'dollars', although the brief's wording (postcode, working days) suggests a UK bank.
The brief does not say whether a numeric date is read day-first or month-first. I used the default 'dmy'.
The brief does not say how to read 'next Friday'. I used the default 'following_week'.
The minimum acceptable amount for every product type is the account field monthly_payment (7.8), so floor_pct is null.
The brief does not require add_note (the API marks it as Brief B), so notes.enabled is false. The note values in events still use the add_note reason enum in case they are needed.
Customers are behind on one product only, so the multi-product settings keep their defaults and do not matter in practice.
If the customer refuses the persuasion offer on the latest allowed date, the call closes as NP-REF (7.9), so refuse_deadline_is_refusal is true.
Customers who still decline security after one explanation get SEC-REF (security_fail/refused). Asking what the call is about counts as declining (default).
For a request to speak to a person, the agent asks once whether it can help, then transfers to queue 'agents' (TR-AGT).
For hardship, the agent offers the Customer Care team (queue 'care'). If accepted the code is TR-CARE, if declined NP-HARD. A reduced-plan request goes to queue 'plans' (TR-PLAN, reason 'plan').
The system is retried once on failure. If it fails twice, the call closes with NP-SYS (7.11).
Saying 'I don't want to talk' twice ends the call (default max_not_talk 2). The brief gives no code for this.
Where 7.1 requires stating that the call is recorded, the opening says 'we record this call'.

The brief prescribes the exact wording of the confirmation question 'Is this {title} {last_name}?' (7.2), 'Shall I go ahead and log that?' (7.10) and 'You'll get an email confirmation shortly.' (7.11). These lines use it word for word.
The brief does not say what happens to the rest of the arrears when the customer pays only the minimum, so offer_floor says nothing about it.
Callback day 'today' is allowed even if today is not a business day, so business_days_only is false. The brief says 'same day' with no business-day limit.
